The permanent statutory basis for Commerce Department controls on dual-use exports. It replaced the Export Administration Act of 1979, which had lapsed and been kept alive for years by emergency declarations. It was enacted as part of the FY2019 defense authorization.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: Pub. L. 115-232](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/115/public/232){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 50 U.S.C. 4801-4852](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/4811?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Authorizes the Export Administration Regulations and the Commerce Control List.
- Sec. 1758: an interagency process to identify and control emerging and foundational technologies.
- Supports end-user controls such as the Entity List.
- Civil and criminal penalties and enforcement authorities.

## Why it matters

It is the legal base for controls on advanced semiconductors and chipmaking tools to China. It ended reliance on [IEEPA](ieepa-1977.qmd) for routine export controls, complements the [Arms Export Control Act](aeca-1976.qmd) on the munitions side, and was paired with [FIRRMA](firrma-2018.qmd) as a two-part response to technology transfer.

## Current status

In force with no sunset.

[Last checked November 10, 2026.]{.checked}

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Framework statute. Standing laws that create institutions or general procedures other laws and executive actions plug into, such as the National Security Act, the War Powers Resolution, IEEPA, and FISA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [IEEPA](ieepa-1977.qmd), [NDAA (annual)](ndaa-annual.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 50 U.S.C.](title50-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Sanctions, cyber, and great powers ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 11: Arms transfers, export controls, and investment screening](../study/units/arms-transfers.qmd) (core reading).
- **Who's involved.** [HFAC](../whos-who.qmd#hfac), [Senate Banking](../whos-who.qmd#senate-banking), [BIS](../whos-who.qmd#bis).
